recent_articles.title: Agri-tech has improved productivity and post-harvest management, say experts at webinar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Experts at a webinar organized by **SRM Institute of Science and Technology** and **The Hindu** discussed the advancements in agricultural technology.  **Dr. Devinder Dhingra**, Principal Scientist (Process Engineering), **ICAR**, highlighted that 47% of farm work is now mechanized, leading to surplus production and exports. **Poorna Pushkala**, CEO of **Samunnati Foundation**, emphasized the role of decentralised energy systems and ad-tech innovations in bolstering the sector.  **Leenus Jesu Martin M.**, Dean of **SRMIST's Faculty of Engineering and Technology**, noted that agriculture is now a multi-disciplinary field with contributions from mechanical, automation, and computing engineers.

recent_articles.title: Rising global costs threaten Mexico’s production costs and food stability | Inflation | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Rising global costs of fuel and fertilizer, driven by shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, are forcing **Mexican** consumers to tighten budgets and cut back on consumption.  The price hikes for staples like tomatoes, potatoes, beef, and chillies have led to increased consumer spending on food and a drop in sales at local markets.  **Elites**, including **Elvira Pasillas**, professor at the Western Institute of Technology and Higher Education (ITESO), are concerned about the impact this will have on low-income households who spend nearly 70 percent of their earnings on food. The rising cost of fuel, roadblocks, and extortion by organized criminal groups are also contributing to higher prices for meat, produce, and other goods.  The Mexican government has implemented a voluntary agreement with retailers to reduce the fuel tax but this is expected to strain public finances.

recent_articles.title: French Open has ‘positive’ meeting with players over tennis dispute | Tennis News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The French Tennis Federation (FFT)** met with representatives of top tennis players on Friday to discuss their demands for greater revenue sharing at Grand Slam tournaments. The meeting, which was described as positive and transparent, resulted in an agreement to continue dialogue and meet again in the coming weeks.  **Roland Garros director Amelie Mauresmo**, who led the FFT delegation, stated that prize money will not change this year. The players involved are seeking a 22 percent share of tournament revenue by 2030 and greater involvement in key decisions regarding Grand Slam tournaments. Representatives from the top players' agents plan to meet with organizers of Wimbledon and the US Open later in the month.

recent_articles.title: ‘Every health facility said they were full’: alarm over rapid spread of Ebola in DRC | Ebola | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)** and **Mercy Corps** have warned that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading rapidly, overwhelming healthcare systems. The virus has claimed nearly 180 lives since its emergence in April, and hospitals are struggling to cope with the influx of suspected cases.  The spread of the disease is exacerbated by cultural practices like funeral wakes, which can facilitate transmission. **Médecins Sans Frontières** (MSF) reports that healthcare facilities are overwhelmed, and there is a shortage of isolation wards.

recent_articles.title: Indian-origin cancer specialist banned from practising in UK says, 'I will never work in that country again' - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Shamir Chandran**, an Indian-origin oncologist, has been struck off the UK medical register after a tribunal ruled that his criminal conviction made him a risk to the public.  The **Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service (MPTS)** found Chandran guilty of controlling and coercive behaviour and cruelty to a person under 16, and he fled the UK before the proceedings. The tribunal deemed allowing Chandran to continue practicing medicine would damage public trust in the profession.

recent_articles.title: White House pauses removal of detainees to the DRC as Ebola outbreak widens | Ebola | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Trump administration** has temporarily paused the removal of refugees to the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) due to a spiraling Ebola outbreak.  Experts argue that this move will not help prevent the spread of the disease, and some fear it could violate international law by sending people back to countries where they may be persecuted. The **US Department of Homeland Security** maintains that it follows health and safety guidelines when conducting removals but did not respond to questions about Zapata's case or future plans for third-country removals during the outbreak.  The **Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)** has implemented screening measures at airports to limit risk, while experts emphasize that travelers from affected areas are unlikely to bring Ebola into the United States.

recent_articles.title: Indian national arrested after $5.6 million meth-making chemical found hidden in food consignment at Sydney port - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Australian Border Force (ABF)** officers seized approximately 166kg of pseudoephedrine, a controlled chemical used in methamphetamine production, from an Indian-origin shipment at Sydney's Port Botany. The man who attempted to collect the consignment was charged with importing a border-controlled precursor under section 307.11(3) of the Criminal Code (Cth). **ABF Superintendent Shaun Baker** highlighted the effectiveness of intelligence-driven operations in preventing drug trafficking.

recent_articles.title: The pollution that outlives war | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The United Nations** and **Ukrainian organizations** have documented thousands of environmental harms caused by the ongoing war, including fires at oil facilities, deforestation, contamination from damaged industrial sites, and widespread risks to water systems.  These incidents are linked to attacks on fuel depots, industrial sites, chemical warehouses, and energy infrastructure, as well as the erosion of oversight in conflict zones. The pollution from these events can persist for years, posing significant health risks to communities living near fossil fuel infrastructure.

recent_articles.title: Extra EU border checks suspended at Dover as travellers face delays in heat | Transport | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **French police** temporarily suspended extra EU border checks at the port of Dover to alleviate long delays caused by the new **EU’s entry-exit system (EES)**.  The EES, which replaced passport stamps with digital registration, was fully operational in April and is used by many countries in the Schengen free movement area. The port of Dover reported wait times exceeding two hours for cross-Channel ferries to France, prompting the police to invoke article 9 clause of the EES regulations, allowing for temporary relaxation of checks. Passengers who missed their ferry crossing due to delays will be able to travel on the next available crossing.

recent_articles.title: Coimbatore girl's murder: police arrested two persons - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Inspector General of Police (West Zone) R.V. Ramya Bharathi** announced the arrest of **K. Karthi** and **R. Mohan**, both residents of Pallapalayam near Coimbatore, in connection with the sexual assault-cum-murder of a 10-year-old girl found near Kannampalayam tank on Friday (May 22, 2026).  The duo confessed to luring the child, sexually assaulting her, and subsequently murdering her in a nearby coconut grove. They were remanded in judicial custody until June 5 and May 27 respectively. **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** expressed shock at the incident and instructed police to conduct a swift investigation. The case has sparked protests from residents demanding justice for the victim.

recent_articles.title: Côte d’Ivoire wary of jihadist threat in north 10 years on from major attack | Côte d’Ivoire | The Guardian
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Al-Qaida-affiliated Jama’at Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin (JNIM)
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Following a 2016 terrorist attack in Grand Bassam, **Côte d’Ivoire** has been working to combat terrorism and address the influx of refugees.  The country's defense minister, **Téné Birahima Ouattara**, stated that security forces have strengthened their vigilance to prevent future attacks. The government has also implemented counter-terrorism initiatives, including a training academy for elite units and development programs in border villages. Despite these efforts, the threat of jihadism persists in neighboring countries like Mali and Burkina Faso, prompting concerns about porous borders and evolving tactics employed by groups like **Al-Qaida-affiliated Jama’at Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin (JNIM)**.

recent_articles.title: Even if the Iran war ended today, US fuel prices aren’t likely to normalize this year | Oil | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** faces backlash in polls due to rising gas prices, which have increased since the US and Israel attacked **Iran**. Experts say it will take several months, possibly years, for prices to return to prewar levels of about $3 a gallon because of damage to energy infrastructure and supply chain issues. While a peace deal could lead to initial price drops, industry experts estimate recovery time could range from six months to two years due to the complexities of restoring oil production and transportation in the Persian Gulf.  The war's impact on fuel prices is likely to remain volatile as long as hostilities continue.

recent_articles.title: Democratic chair faces calls to quit over ‘shambles’ of election autopsy release | Democrats | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ken Martin**, chair of the **Democratic National Committee (DNC)**, faces calls to resign following the release of a flawed autopsy report on the 2024 presidential election. The report, which omitted key information and lacked oversight, has deepened concerns about Martin's leadership and sparked criticism from Democratic members of Congress and party leaders.  Several voices have called for his resignation, including **Seth Moulton**, **Marc Veasey**, and **Mark Pocan**.  **Norm Solomon** and **Amanda Litman** also expressed their dissatisfaction with the report and Martin's handling of it. The **Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC)** has launched a campaign to pressure state chairs to call for Martin's resignation, while others have suggested potential successors like **Jane Kleeb** and **Ben Wikler**.

recent_articles.title: UK’s ‘anxious generation’ of young people struggling to adapt to workplace | Young people | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Alan Milburn**, a former Labour health secretary, will release a report this week highlighting the struggles of **young people** in adapting to the current job market.  His review, commissioned by Prime Minister **Keir Starmer**, suggests that a rising tide of mental health issues and social media's influence are contributing factors to high economic inactivity among young adults. The report emphasizes that these young people face unique challenges due to their digital-native upbringing and calls for businesses to offer more flexibility and mental health support to address this issue.  This is expected to impact the government's approach to attracting skilled labor amid falling immigration rates.
